column1: # Rows db.rpstbn.* (line PS, series PR, PS12a, DECISIONS 38): rpstblastn against the profile databases tests/db_search/rps/ (the rps-gz: cell of the db.rps.* rows), queries tests/fasta/rps/{nq,nedge,odd}.fna (build_nq.py there): -comp_based_stats 0 (no composition-based statistics) and the default 1, 2 and 3 (rows c1.*, c2.*, c3.*, PS12b: the redo per frame), the frames, strands, genetic codes, masks, -query_loc, X-drops, window, volumes, -searchsp/OLD_FSC/-dbsize, -max_hsps, -qcov_hsp_perc, -max_target_seqs and outfmt 0/6/7/10; NCBI's -help, its warning of an empty query file, its errors of a missing .aux and of an empty one (rps_mini!aux=empty.aux), its options errors of -ungapped with composition-based statistics, of -xdrop_ungap 0 and of -outfmt 13, 14 and 17, the batches without a valid frame (nedge.fna cut by -query_loc 1-2: inv.*, on three volumes inv3v.*, without .aux noaux.inv); rows rej.* are LOSAT's refusals (outfmt 5 until PS15a, NCBI's crash of -ungapped without them and its undefined -sum_stats true, -subject, a CHUNK_SIZE that NCBI cannot convert). Rows win* (PS12s, DECISIONS 50): BATCH_SIZE 200 or 100 with nwin.fna and nwin0.fna, so that the query batches are many and 1, 2, 4 and 8 threads search them in windows of different batches. Rows b1.* and rej.s1 (PS12s review B1 and S1, nfirst.fna): a first query batch without a valid frame before a batch that LOSAT refuses at a volume, then a later volume's missing file; a query's cutoff refusal after an earlier query's search error in the same batch.

# Rows db.rpstbn.chunkx and db.envconv.rpstblastn.* (env parity H): a CHUNK_SIZE or PRE_FETCH_SEQS_LIMIT that NStr::StringToInt (flags 0) cannot convert: NCBI's rpstblastn stops with its CStringException (CATCH_ALL: 'Error: ' and its report naming ncbistr.cpp in the official release's build tree, exit 255) where it reads the value: CHUNK_SIZE in the set-up of the first query batch (local_blast.cpp:59-61; a value it converts changes nothing, RPS-BLAST is never split, split_query_aux_priv.cpp:88, and OVERLAP_CHUNK_SIZE is never read), PRE_FETCH_SEQS_LIMIT before the first batch's report (blast_app_util.cpp:732-734; not with outfmt 11) (env-parity-20261108/s6_rpstbn).

# Rows db.rpstbn.wide.* and db.rpstbn.ungrouped.* (line PS, series PR, PS12m): rpstblastn against rps_wide (one profile of 133,000 columns, 65 buckets of 2,048 rows: two groups in LOSAT's scan, of 64 buckets and of one; tests/db_search/rps/build_wide.py) and against rps_wide_ug.loo, its table with the hits of the nine cells not in ascending order (put in place of its .loo: !loo=rps_wide_ug.loo.gz); queries tests/fasta/rps/wide.{faa,fna}. NCBI's bytes are equal for both tables; LOSAT regroups the cells when it opens the volume.

# Rows db.rpstbn.{1v,2v,3v}.*, db.rpstbn.{empty,nolet}.*, db.rpstbn.fo11.e5.6 and db.rpstbn.rej.{l0,nm300,fo22,l563n0.oldfsc} (line RG, series D, D1a-3 review 7 S1 and D1a-4 parts A and B and fix round 1): rpstblastn through the rps-gz: cell's alias file (@ALIAS), the search units of rpsblast.tsv's rows db.rps.{1v,2v,3v}.* (one owner, rps_search::volumes::RpsUnits), frozen from NCBI BLAST+ 2.17.0.

# Rows db.rpstbn.qa.* (line RG, T3c): -outfmt 1 to 4 of rpstblastn, which BLASTX's report writes (the frame groups of the queries' frames, the profiles labelled by their CDD ids). Freeze them alone with `freeze --only db.rpstbn.qa`.

# Rows db.rpstbn.dup.* (line RG, series D, D1a-4 fix round 2): a profile that two volumes share, -db "rps_mini3v dup/rps_mini3v.01" (cell rps-gz:rps_mini3v+dup/rps_mini3v.01, a copy of rps_mini3v.01 under its own base name in dup/): NCBI's formatter cuts each query's merged list to the hit list size counting following Seq-aligns whose Seq-ids match as one subject (PruneSeqalign), so both copies of gnl|CDD|102 are written (common::database::joined_cut, both programs)

# Rows db.rpstbn.k.*, cst.*, two0.*, locm.*, c1.oldfscminus.6, c1.spminus.6 and s5e.* (line PS, series PR, PS12b review R1, R2, B1, B2 and S5): the footer K of a batch's highest profile (BATCH_SIZE 200 and 3000 over nq.fna); NCBI's old near-identical test where the query's frame +1 is invalid (cst.fna with -strand minus: cstdq and cstdq2 hold frame -1's consensus without one residue, and the letters that NCBI's redo reads for its window hold the same copy and a Q run, which SEG masks after the old test only; cstq, without the deletion, and cstd, without the Q run, are controls); a redo whose gapped start lies past its window's copy (NCBI's found_end FALSE; two0.fna, CDD:101 in frame +2 and CDD:102 in frame +3, tk_m2.fna, nwin.fna), whose reports print the edit script's ends; with -strand minus -searchsp, frames +1 to +3 of each batch's first query, below NCBI's first context, keep search space 0 (redo e-values 0). With one strand NCBI's redo reads its frames with the six-frame arithmetic of GET_NUCL_LENGTH (D5), so a window can hold another frame's letters: NCBI's two0 output shows a frame +3 hit scored on frame +2's letters, and LOSAT's is the same (not a LOSAT defect). cst.fna, two0.fna and tk_m2.fna (tests/fasta/rps/) are the PS12b review's seeded probe inputs. s5e.fna (one record of the seeded queries of the S5 search, PR/ws/ps12b/ps12b_s5gen.py) has, with -strand minus, a found_end FALSE HSP whose own ends lie before its starts: NCBI sorts the HSPs and computes qcovhsp on those ends (0 here) and prints the rows of the edit script.
# Rows db.xj.rpstbn.* (K4j): rpstblastn reads its queries with BLASTX's reader: query titles with a Latin-1 and an undecodable byte (tests/db_search/xj/xj_rps_l1.fna).

# Rows db.rpstbn.stdin.* (RL4 fix/stdin-ncbi-cin): the query from standard input (`-query -`, query cell stdin:): an empty pipe with outfmt 0 to 4 gives NCBI's epilog up to 'Matrix: ' (no query batch named the database's matrix, CreateRpsStructures), 'BLAST failed to write output', rc 6, and outfmt 7 counts 0 queries; eol_lost_g55 (tests/fixtures/fasta_input) through a pipe and as a redirected file keeps the tail that NCBI's cin reads one byte per refill (Length=107), and named by its path loses it (Length=85, row stdin.g55.path).

# Rows db.dlm.ps.*, db.dlm.rps.*, db.dlm.rpst.*, db.dlm.bp.* and db.dlm.tbnp.* (line RG, series F, item D-36 and its reviews 1 and 1b): psiblast's, rpsblast's and rpstblastn's custom delimiter (-outfmt "6|7|10|20 delim=X ..."), which their applications never hand to the formatter (psiblast_app.cpp:501-505, rpsblast_app.cpp:186-189, rpstblastn_app.cpp:183-186: no SetCustomDelimiter, which blastp_app.cpp:249 calls): NCBI 2.17.0 writes the format's own delimiter (the comma of outfmt 10 and 20 and their header line, the tab of 6 and 7; `6 delim=@` and `7 delim=,` are the default reports, whose identities rpsblast counts on the letters as read) and still checks delim= against the fields (s_ValidateCustomDelim, rc 1, before LOSAT's refusal of rpsblast's and rpstblastn's outfmt 20, item PS15a); a format number with a leading zero or a plus sign (`06`, `+6`, `00`: NStr::StringToInt, blast_args.cpp:2829) and the words after outfmt 0 to 4, which NCBI drops (blast_args.cpp:2845-2851), on the command line and in the library, blastp's rows (db.dlm.bp.*) too; outfmt 13 and 14 without -out: NCBI's `Please provide a file name` (UseXInclude, blast_app_util.cpp:888-899; none after `Query is Empty!`) before LOSAT's refusals of psiblast's, rpsblast's and PSI-TBLASTN's outfmt 13 and 14 (items PS15a, PS15b); FASTA queries of tests/fasta/psiblast/ against tests/db_search/paja (one and two rounds, no hit, a database without sequences, an empty query file), the PSSMs tests/fixtures/pssm/ps4_tk_paja.asn.gz (outfmt 6 and 7: LOSAT refuses its 10 and 20, item PS15b) and ps7_ts1_tslice.asn.gz (PSI-TBLASTN against tests/db_search/tslice) and the scaled PSSM that NCBI stops at after the prolog; rpsblast's and rpstblastn's against rps_mini (outfmt 20 only with a delimiter that its fields use: LOSAT's RPS programs refuse it otherwise). The command line and the library read one rule (report::tabular::TabularSpec::of_app; app::ncbi_refuses_format); probes F/d36/probe of remaining-gaps-20261112.

# Rows db.rpstbn.*.c1, *.c2 and *.c3 (line RG, series D, D1a-4 fix round 8: the merge of dev with PS12b): D1a-4's rows (all -comp_based_stats 0) with composition-based statistics: every row with the default, 1 (the option left out), one row of each mechanism with 2 or 3 (the units' Gumbel blocks under NCBI's 5 x E-value of the preliminary stage, OLD_FSC without it, the joined cut, the footer K of the first unit, the OID range's unlisted HSPs), and LENGTH 400 over one volume with 2 and 3, where that E-value keeps two alignments past the concatenated length and NCBI's interval tree splits without end (NCBI: 'BLAST ran out of memory', exit 4, under an 8 GiB limit): LOSAT's refusal of db.rpstbn.rej.l0's class. Frozen from NCBI BLAST+ 2.17.0.

# Rows db.rpstbn.of8.lcm to db.rpstbn.of20.qloc, db.rpstbn.of{8,18}.col, db.rpstbn.of20{n,id,tx}.col, db.rpstbn.rej.of{15,20,20q}col, db.rpstbn.rej.of{18,20tx}coltax, db.rpstbn.of*.tax* and db.rpstbn.of{15,18}.v3n (line PS, series PR, PS15a-2): the formats that rpstblastn adds through BLASTX's writers, one row each (8, 9, 12 to 16, 18, 20), with -lcase_masking for the identity counts (as rpsblast's rows db.rps.of*), the documents' query_frame, a query without alignments (-strand minus) and three volumes cut to one profile per query (v3m). Rows *.col: rpscol's entry lcl|Query_1: NCBI's bytes where the report names ids only or reads nothing of the entry or the alignment, LOSAT's refusals where NCBI takes the query for it or stops with an exception (13 to 16, 18 of a profile with a taxid, 20 with fields that show more of the entry than its id or open the alignment block; *coltax: the same profile with the taxid 9606). Rows *.tax (review S2) and v3n (review B1): as rpsblast's rows db.rps.of*.tax* and db.rps.of15.v3x. Frozen from NCBI BLAST+ 2.17.0.

# Rows db.hitlist.* (line NP, O1c): RPSTBLASTN with a -max_target_seqs whose preliminary size (2*h+50 with composition-based statistics) passes NCBI's int: NCBI wraps 2147483624 to 2 and keeps 2 profiles per query; LOSAT computes the size without the overflow (PD-LOSAT-NCBI-DEFECTS exception 19) and keeps every hit, NCBI's run at 1073741798 (the `ncbi-near` row near.6).

# Rows db.rpstbn.sw.* and db.rpstbn.rej.swendless* (line PS, series PR, PS12c and PS12d): -use_sw_tback with composition-based statistics 1, 2 and 3: NCBI's Smith-Waterman redo of each profile's matches in the windows of each frame (Blast_RedoOneMatchSmithWaterman per window: the window's composition adjustment, score-only scans with forbidden ranges, the start and the X-drop traceback; PS11c-3's kernels on PS12b's windows), at -comp_based_stats 0 the bytes without it (NCBI's traceback does not read it), on three volumes, with -strand plus and minus, -searchsp, -seg, -window_size 0, outfmt 0, 6, 7 and 11. rej.swendless*: a significant score of 0 whose first cell scores above 0 in a window of two or more HSPs, where NCBI repeats the redo without end (PD-LOSAT-NCBI-DEFECTS 1.30, 1.80): tks_m.fna (tkcut570's frame +1 from tks_M, M first) with -evalue 1e4, and nq.fna with -strand minus (frame +1 invalid: the redo's search space 0, every score significant); tks_m.fna with -strand plus and with -evalue 100, tks_w.fna (W first) with -strand plus, and both with -strand minus (no hit: every profile's redo fails) end. Rows sw.nest.* (PS12d): nest_p.fna, nest_m.fna (minus strand) and nest_pm.fna (both, two queries of one batch), whose second alignment of the redo starts with 95 gaps in the profile's row: its Std-seg's first segment has no location in that row, so `CSeq_align::GetSeqRange` of the profile's row throws (Row seqids not consistent) where a report reads it (PD-LOSAT-NCBI-DEFECTS rule 2, written as NCBI's): the prefetch warns (not in outfmt 8, 9, 11 and 12, nor with PRE_FETCH_SEQS_LIMIT=0), outfmt 0 to 4 stop at the description table (exit status 255), as do 13 and 14, BLAST XML, JSON and XML2 stop their document with the exception (exit status 0), and outfmt 0 to 4 without the description table (-num_descriptions 0) write the alignments, outfmt 0 the leading gap as spaces; the formats, -num_descriptions 0, -num_alignments, -line_length, -sorthits and -sorthsps (which rpstblastn's formatter does not take: rpstblastn_app.cpp sets no sort option), -max_target_seqs, -max_hsps, PRE_FETCH_SEQS_LIMIT=0 and -comp_based_stats 2 and 3.
